fixes.explanation: Stars it is. Jesus tells John that the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches (Revelation 1:20). So these words to Ephesus come from the One who holds them in His right hand and walks among the seven golden lampstands. I need my whole mustache just to carry ONE cookie box without a wobble.

Not this time. Jesus says they "…tested and exposed as liars those who falsely claim to be apostles." That's what He tells us Ephesus did with them. The text doesn't say anything about letting them teach.

Yes. Jesus says they have persevered and endured many things "…for the sake of My name." And He says they did it "Without growing weary." I get tired just stamping one batch, so that's a lot to admire.
The text doesn't say that. Jesus says they endured "…for the sake of My name." He gives one reason, and it isn't the city. His name is the reason on the page.
The text never says this. Jesus' complaint is, "You have abandoned your first love." Nothing about their meetings comes up. I'd hate to hand Jesus a complaint He never made, friend.

Lampstand is right. Jesus says, "But if you do not repent, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place." Notice the "if" in that warning. Earlier He tells John the seven lampstands are the seven churches (Revelation 1:20), so He's speaking to a church about its own lampstand.

A crown does show up in this passage, but it's in the Smyrna letter, where Jesus promises "…the crown of life." For Ephesus, the warning is about a lampstand. Jesus says, "But if you do not repent, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place."

No altar in this verse, friend. Jesus says, "But if you do not repent, I will come to you and remove your lampstand from its place." The seven lampstands are the seven churches (Revelation 1:20). So the warning is about that lampstand, and it depends on whether they repent.

That's a different tree. The tree of the knowledge of good and evil is in Genesis 2:17. The promise here is the right to eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God. Jesus makes that promise to the one who overcomes.

Good guess, baker, but hidden manna isn't in this passage. Here Jesus promises the one who overcomes the right to eat from the tree of life in the Paradise of God. That's the promise on the page. And the story isn't over.
